purpose: Read every tracked working-tree file; enumerate finite proof candidates; detect declared Lean lexical trust/placeholder tokens and explicitly classified float-certification patterns; surface all unsupported or inaccessible coverage.

outputs.selftest: JSON, exit 0 iff baseline passes and exact finite mutation threshold is met
outputs.scan: JSON, exit 1 active findings; exit 2 missing semantics/coverage; never claims overall Layer A PASS

quarantine_policy: Exact SHA256 matching requires statement, reason, attempts, owner:none; annotate and preserve every finding; independent isolation and CLOSED-dependency audit required. Scanner never suppresses active findings.
limitations: Not a Lean parser, kernel, theorem statement alignment checker, nonvacuity proof, or transitive axiom closure checker.
Candidate inventory is finite extension detection plus explicit proof-source registry; semantic classification must cover arbitrarily encoded or embedded proof sources.
Archives are hashed and explicitly unscanned; inner members are not claimed examined.
Python float detector covers AST float/complex literals and direct float or listed attribute calls, not arbitrary aliasing or FFI; Lean float detector covers Float/Float32/Float64 tokens.
No default classification treats UI Float use as mathematical certification; registry completeness remains semantic work.
Working-tree byte inventory is not an atomic snapshot or a commit/build receipt.
No A4 bound preservation, A5 test-preservation/regression, or A6 nonvacuity conclusion is inferred from token counts.
